To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel approach to learning modular scene models by training an ensemble (competition) of generative models.

we present an alternative to current unsupervised generative models of scenes by training an ensemble (i.e. competition) of experts that learn to specialize on different object classes and recombine them in physically plausible ways.

we propose an approach for unsupervised learning that allows for controllable and physically plausible sampling of individual objects, and recombination of objects into new scenes, which can be used to generate novel scenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how we can learn to model complex scenes with a modular representation.
learning a generative scene model that can be used to generate new scenes with novel arrangements of objects and to recombine parts of existing scenes in a physically plausible way.
the question: How to build a generative model of complex scenes which is modular, causal, interpretable, and can recombine its building blocks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model is the first to learn a modular and compositional representation of visual scenes.
the authors propose a method for unsupervised learning that allows for the recombination of objects in a physically plausible way.
the proposed model is a first step towards a causal generative model of complex scenes, which can learn to recombine objects in a physically plausible manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a new way to learn generative scene models, that is based on a competition of experts.
the proposed approach allows to generate novel object arrangements and depth ordering in physically plausible ways, and that it is a step towards learning causal generative scene representations.
we are able to learn a set of experts that can explain different aspects of the scene, and then we can combine these experts in different ways to generate a scene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a modular representation of the visual world can emerge through competition between experts, without the need of supervision or a global object detector.
the competition of multiple experts can help learn a modular and hierarchical representation of complex data, which can be useful in many applications.
the competition of experts can be used to learn object-based representations in a modular way.
